script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'globe-sources-a',
  description: 'Live-verify NASA GIBS GOES tiles, NOAA GOES on AWS and MRMS 3D reflectivity, then refute each report',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'live request + content check per source' },
    { title: 'Refute', detail: 'independent re-check of each report' },
  ],
}

const SCRATCH = '/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RoofingApp/7638440a-a008-5ef8-a289-86be0a23e7a7/scratchpad'
const EVID = '/home/user/RoofingApp/research/globe/validation-evidence/'

const CTX = `You are one of several agents building the "globe view" research scaffold for RoofingApp (a Montana roofing company's weather desktop app). A supervisor reads your output; it is data, not prose for a person.

Repo: /home/user/RoofingApp. First read /home/user/RoofingApp/research/globe/README.md sections 1-7 (the plan); your workstream is in section 5.

Rules that bind you (from AGENTS.md):
- Rule 7: make the live request AND check the content. Decode the tile or file and report what is inside (pixel stats, variable names, grid dimensions). HTTP 200 proves nothing.
- Rule 9: no "best" claims; comparisons with evidence only.
- Rule 5: observation, satellite estimate, radar estimate and official alert stay separate; never "confirmed damage".

Working rules:
- Today is 2026-10-17 (UTC); day-of-year 290. Outbound HTTPS works through a preconfigured proxy (Python requests and curl honour it). pip install works; you may install packages for research and must list them in your result. Never edit requirements.txt.
- Downloads go into a fresh empty directory ${SCRATCH}/globe-dl/<your-slug>/ . Scripts you write go in ${SCRATCH}/globe-scripts/<your-slug>/ and read downloads by path; run them with "python -I".
- Montana bounding box: lon -116.05 to -104.04, lat 44.36 to 49.00. Billings: 45.7833, -108.5007.
- Write ONLY the files your task names. Your evidence file goes in ${EVID} as JSON of at most 20 KB: no binary captures, no large response bodies (every crew machine downloads the repo zipball, so research artifacts must stay small).
- Never write model names or AI-vendor identifiers into any file.
- Do not modify payload/, desktop/, tests/, docs/, or research/globe/README.md.
- For documentation and terms pages use WebFetch or WebSearch (load them with ToolSearch "select:WebFetch,WebSearch"). Quote the exact sentence you rely on, with its URL.
- If something cannot be verified, write "unverified" and why. Never guess a number.

Evidence file shape (JSON):
{
  "workstream": "W#", "slug": "...", "checked_at_utc": "...",
  "urls_checked": [{"url": "...", "method": "GET", "status": 200, "bytes": 0, "content_type": "...", "cors_allow_origin": "... or null", "content_check": "what you decoded and what it showed", "verified": true}],
  "facts": [{"claim": "...", "value": "...", "evidence": "url or file", "verified": true}],
  "terms": {"license": "...", "attribution_required": true, "quote": "...", "url": "..."},
  "limits": ["..."], "installed_packages": ["..."], "open_questions": ["..."]
}`

const SRC = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    slug: { type: 'string' },
    evidence_file: { type: 'string' },
    headline_facts: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    blockers: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    installed_packages: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    confidence: { type: 'string', enum: ['high', 'medium', 'low'] },
  },
  required: ['slug', 'evidence_file', 'headline_facts', 'blockers', 'confidence'],
}

const REV = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    slug: { type: 'string' },
    refuted_claims: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    corrections: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    confirmed: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    unverified: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    evidence_file_updated: { type: 'boolean' },
  },
  required: ['slug', 'refuted_claims', 'corrections', 'confirmed', 'unverified', 'evidence_file_updated'],
}

const ITEMS = [
  {
    slug: 'gibs', title: 'W1 NASA GIBS WMTS: GOES GeoColor / Band 13, Blue Marble, VIIRS true colour',
    task: `1. Fetch https://gibs.earthdata.nasa.gov/wmts/epsg3857/best/1.0.0/WMTSCapabilities.xml (and the epsg4326 one). Parse it (xml.etree). List every layer whose identifier contains "GOES" (expect names like GOES-East_ABI_GeoColor, GOES-East_ABI_Band13_Clean_Infrared, GOES-West_ABI_GeoColor), plus BlueMarble_ShadedRelief_Bathymetry, VIIRS_SNPP_CorrectedReflectance_TrueColor, VIIRS_NOAA20_CorrectedReflectance_TrueColor. For each: TileMatrixSet(s), format, Dimension time (default value, the time period such as PT10M, the start of the available range), ResourceURL template.
2. For a GOES GeoColor layer and a Band 13 layer: fetch a tile over Montana (zoom 5 in the GoogleMapsCompatible scheme covers lon -110 lat 47 at roughly x=6, y=11 - compute it yourself and show the formula) at the default time and at the previous time step. Decode with PIL: size, mode, percent of non-transparent pixels, number of distinct colours, mean RGB. A tile that is fully transparent or one flat colour is NOT verified imagery - say so.
3. Measure latency: latest available time in the capabilities versus now (UTC). Measure the update period from the dimension.
4. Record the CORS header (Access-Control-Allow-Origin) on a tile GET sent with an Origin header, because the globe fetches tiles from inside a browser page.
5. Find and quote GIBS terms/citation and any usage limits, and the GOES layers' native resolution and whether GIBS GOES imagery is parallax-corrected (search GIBS layer documentation; if nothing says so, write unverified).
Write ${EVID}gibs.json.`,
  },
  {
    slug: 'goes-aws', title: 'W2 NOAA GOES-East/West on AWS: band 13 imagery, ACHA cloud-top height, cloud optical depth',
    task: `Buckets: noaa-goes19 (GOES-East since 2025 - verify by listing recent data), noaa-goes18 (GOES-West), and check whether noaa-goes16 still receives new data. Use the S3 REST listing: https://noaa-goes19.s3.amazonaws.com/?list-type=2&prefix=ABI-L2-ACHAC/2026/290/ then narrow to the latest hour.
1. For products ABI-L2-ACHAC (cloud top height, CONUS), ABI-L2-CMIPC (band 13 only: files containing M6C13 or M3C13), ABI-L2-CODC (cloud optical depth), ABI-L2-ACTPC (cloud phase): list the latest files, decode the s/e/c timestamps in the names, record file sizes, and derive the cadence from consecutive files (expect 5 minutes for CONUS). Also record one ABI-L2-MCMIPC (all bands) size and one full-disk ACHAF size for comparison.
2. Download the latest ACHAC file and the matching CMIPC band 13 file into the download directory. pip install netCDF4 (and h5netcdf if needed). Open each: list variables (expect HT, DQF, x, y, t, goes_imager_projection), units (HT in metres, CMI in kelvin), _FillValue, scale_factor/add_offset, valid_range, grid shape (CONUS 2 km is 1500 x 2500), time attributes (time_coverage_start/end).
3. Compute latitude/longitude for the grid from the geostationary projection attributes (perspective_point_height, semi_major_axis, semi_minor_axis, longitude_of_projection_origin) with numpy - the standard GOES fixed-grid formulas. Report the fraction of valid cloud-top-height cells inside the Montana bounding box and the 10/50/90th percentile height there, plus the fraction flagged by DQF. Report the band 13 brightness temperature range over Montana.
4. Latency: now minus the file's time_coverage_end at listing time. Bytes per 5-minute step for the three CONUS products you would need (ACHAC + CMIPC C13 + CODC).
5. CORS: GET one object with an Origin header; record Access-Control-Allow-Origin (or its absence).
6. Terms: quote the licence statement from https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-goes/ (NOAA Open Data Dissemination) and the GOES-R Product Definition and Users' Guide note that ACHA is a retrieval (an estimate) if you can find it; else unverified.
Write ${EVID}goes-aws.json.`,
  },
  {
    slug: 'mrms', title: 'W3 MRMS on AWS: 3D MergedReflectivityQC (33 heights), composite, MESH, coverage products',
    task: `Bucket noaa-mrms-pds. Start with https://noaa-mrms-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/?list-type=2&prefix=CONUS/&delimiter=/ to enumerate product prefixes.
1. List every MergedReflectivityQC_XX.XX level present (expect 33 from 00.50 to 19.00 km). For the latest common timestamp list the file name and gz size per level, and sum them: bytes per 2-minute step for the full 3D mosaic. Also list latest file and size for MergedReflectivityQCComposite_00.50, MESH_00.50, MESH_Max_60min_00.50 (or whatever MESH max products exist), ReflectivityAtLowestAltitude_00.50, RadarQualityIndex_00.50, EchoTop_18_00.50, VIL_00.50, and any product whose name suggests radar coverage or quality (list all names you see that contain Quality, Coverage, Mask).
2. Download the latest files for levels 00.50, 03.00, 06.00 and 10.00 and the MESH_00.50 file. gunzip them. Decode GRIB2: pip install eccodes (binary wheels include the library); import eccodes and read keys Ni, Nj, latitudeOfFirstGridPointInDegrees, longitudeOfFirstGridPointInDegrees, latitudeOfLastGridPointInDegrees, longitudeOfLastGridPointInDegrees, iDirectionIncrementInDegrees, jDirectionIncrementInDegrees, dataDate, dataTime, and the values array. If eccodes fails, try pip install cfgrib xarray (xr.open_dataset(path, engine='cfgrib')) or pygrib; record every failure message verbatim. Expect a 7000 x 3500 grid at 0.01 degrees covering lon -129.995..-60.005, lat 54.995..20.005.
3. From the decoded values: the distinct negative sentinel values and their counts (MRMS uses one code for "missing" and another for "no radar coverage" - identify which is which from the NSSL MRMS GRIB2 tables at https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/projects/mrms/operational/tables.php or the MRMS operational product guide; quote). For the Montana bounding box at each decoded level: percent of cells with no coverage, percent missing, percent >= 20 dBZ and >= 35 dBZ, max dBZ. For MESH: units (mm) and max over Montana. The no-coverage percentages are the Montana radar gaps the plan warns about - report them exactly.
4. Cadence from consecutive file timestamps; latency = now minus latest file time. CORS header on one object GET with an Origin header.
5. Terms: quote the licence statement from https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-mrms-pds/ . Note the MRMS version if the files or docs state it.
Write ${EVID}mrms.json.`,
  },
]

function researchPrompt(it) {
  return CTX + '\n\n# Your workstream: ' + it.title + '\n\n' + it.task +
    '\n\nWhen done, return: slug, evidence_file (absolute path), headline_facts (the 5-10 facts that matter for the plan, each with its number and unit), blockers (anything you could not do, with the exact error), installed_packages, confidence.'
}

function refutePrompt(it, res) {
  return CTX + '\n\n# Your job: REFUTE the report for ' + it.title +
    '\n\nA previous agent wrote ' + EVID + it.slug + '.json and summarised it as:\n' + JSON.stringify(res, null, 2) +
    '\n\nRead the evidence file. Then independently re-check every fact that matters to the plan, using different inputs where possible (a different tile, time step, level or file than the first agent used), and re-read each quoted terms page yourself. Default to suspicion: a claim with no decoded content behind it is unverified; a number copied from memory is unverified. Check especially: cadence, latency, bytes per step, grid dimensions, sentinel values, CORS headers, licence wording, and any claim about parallax or resolution.' +
    '\n\nThen UPDATE the evidence file in place: fix wrong values in "facts" and add "corrected_by_review": true to each one you changed; add a top-level "review" object {"refuted_claims": [...], "corrections": [...], "confirmed": [...], "unverified": [...], "reviewer_checks": [{"url": "...", "content_check": "...", "verified": true}]}. Keep the file at or under 20 KB. Return the same lists plus evidence_file_updated.'
}

log('Wave 1A: verifying GIBS, GOES on AWS, MRMS - each report then refuted')
const results = await pipeline(ITEMS,
  it => agent(researchPrompt(it), { label: 'verify:' + it.slug, phase: 'Verify', model: WORKER, schema: SRC }),
  (res, it) => res ? agent(refutePrompt(it, res), { label: 'refute:' + it.slug, phase: 'Refute', model: WORKER, schema: REV }) : null,
)
return { slugs: ITEMS.map(i => i.slug), reviews: results }

refuted_claims: GOES-West GeoColor 01:00Z missing: now 200 with stable bytes, and listed.
Off-grid returns the previous frame (uniform rule): not uniform; exact off-grid frames exist.
Capabilities cannot give the latest frame: KVP with no TIME returns the newest 10-min frame (not every exact label).
Frame size 48-97 KB per tile: observed 33-141 KB.
GOES-East Band 13 served from about 07-16: noon 07-16 and 07-17 are 404; first 200 at 07-18.
SNPP runs through 10-16: capabilities list 10-17 (black sentinel).
Bulk: 48 h, 50 Mbps and 500 threads are requirements: the page gives a request and guidelines.
corrections: Limits are TM6 (GeoColor) and TM5 (Band13); server serves TM7 and TM6. Use the served result.
1.22 and 2.45 km are tile-grid sizes at the equator (x0.68 at 47 N), not native.
Latency 19-45 min in the poll sample; late frames 76-96 min after label; Band 13 sooner than GeoColor here.
Served layers are *_v0_NRT (3.5 h class): verified.
Band 13 2 km verified by netCDF attribute (G19, G18).
An exact 5-min label can carry a scan 5 min earlier (BW 02:15Z = 02:10:20Z scan; 02:35Z = 02:30:20Z).
Parallax: now supported for 5 frames (zero shift); cloud-height untested.
VIIRS: PT6M granule layers exist; SNPP 10-17 is a black sentinel too.
confirmed: Tile sizes 256/512 px; TMS names; 4326 TM5 40x20 (9 deg per tile).
Montana z5 x6 y11 bounds; decoded colour counts GE 01:00Z, BE 01:20Z, GW 01:10Z, VIIRS 10-16.
Off-grid GE 00:03Z = 00:00Z bytes; 02:03Z and 02:07Z = 02:00Z bytes.
June 2025 Domain PT10M with tiles 404; VIIRS 10-17 black sentinel.
CORS ACAO * on every response tested; OPTIONS without Allow-Methods.
GeoColor 1 km, ~40 min; NASA CC0, NOAA NODD and GIBS acknowledgment quotes.
unverified: Satellite behind GeoColor (RGB); source of the GE 02:15Z frame.
VIIRS granule content; VIIRS and Blue Marble licences beyond the NASA default; derived GeoColor licence.
Latency beyond the poll sample; guide band chart (link only).

refuted_claims: GOES-16 newest CMIPC object 2025-04-07T05:19:17Z: refuted. The newest CMIPC scan (band 13 included) was uploaded 2025-04-07T18:37:11Z.

CODC percent_good_quality_qf 0.645 does not reproduce from the DQF bits: refuted. It reproduces exactly as good (DQF bit 4 clear) cells over non-fill DQF cells (2,390,092 / 3,702,838 = 0.645476). The 0.443 figure uses valid COD cells as the denominator.
A 2 km ACHA grid contradicts the 10 km ACHAC file: refuted as a contradiction. The 2 km product is ABI-L2-ACHA2KMC (1500 x 2500), present since 2023-03-24; ACHAC stayed 10 km.

Latency ranges (MCMIPC 21-35 s, C13 27-39 s, ACHAF 146-161 s, CODC median 145 s, ACHAC median 115 s) are one-hour ranges. Over 24 GOES-19 scans: MCMIPC 19.0-44.2 s, C13 26.1-46.1 s, ACHAF 145.5-177.5 s, CODC median 148.8 s, ACHAC median 114.8 s.
One MCMIPC file 38.8-40.2 MB (median 39.4 MB) is refuted for 24 files, which give 38.6-44.2 MB (median 40.3 MB).
Valid height exactly where DQF=0, as a general rule: true for the 10 km ACHAC only. False for ACHA2KMC, which has heights at all DQF 1 cells and some DQF 2 cells.
All valid COD cells use the night algorithm, as a general rule: true for the 01:41 scene only. At 00:01, 17.1% of valid cells are day-algorithm.
File extent -150.62 W 'from image bounds': not reproduced (pixel-edge minimum -150.97, pixel-centre -151.41, file attribute -152.11).
corrections: Two cloud-top height products exist: ACHAC 10 km (300 x 500; 0.32 MB per 5-min step, GOES-19) and ACHA2KMC 2 km (1500 x 2500; 4.44-4.50 MB per step GOES-19; 4.23-4.46 MB GOES-18). The plan's resolution and byte budget must cover both.

Bytes: GOES-19 ACHAC+C13+CODC median 7,479,721 bytes per step (confirmed). GOES-18 median 8,618,768 (the first report's 8,682,798 is not reproduced). With ACHA2KMC in place of ACHAC: about 11.6 MB per step on GOES-19.
GOES-18 latencies are shorter than the first report's GOES-19-only figures: ACHAC median 98.0 s, C13 32.8 s, CODC 117.0 s, MCMIPC 27.8 s, ACHAF 91.7 s.
Montana valid height: 733 of 1,777 = 41.25% (one decimal 41.2%, not 41.3%). p90 is 13,078.5 m by linear interpolation (13,079 is rounding).

COD saturates: 215,429 valid CONUS cells (11.0%) sit at raw code 6553 (= 16.0) on the 01:41 scene, so the 16.0 maximum is a cap (cause unverified). 'All night' holds at 01:41 only; at 00:01, 17.1% of valid cells are day.
DQF: 2026 files show codes 0-3 and 255 (code 4 not observed); the 2023-03-11 v01r00 file has codes 4 and 6. Compare DQF history by algorithm version only.

README section 4 parallax wording 'tens of km poleward' overstates for tops up to 10 km. Spherical WGS84 geometry: a 10 km top displaces 17-19 km (GOES-19 toward 317 deg, NW; GOES-18 toward 37 deg, NE), with about 14 km north in both; a 12 km top gives 21-23 km. The first report's flat-Earth figures (18.8 / 17.1 km) agree within 0.2 km.

10 km HT averaging conflict: ATBD v3.0 section 1.11.3 (PDF page 41) says good-quality 2 km pixels are averaged over 5x5 blocks for 10 km products; file HT cell_methods say 'area: point' (also in the 2023 file).

Licence: the data.gov ACHA catalog entry gives CC0 1.0, accessLevel non-public, rights otherRestrictions. The NOAA NODD program page does not carry the registry sentence. The registry sentence (summarising fetch) is the only NOAA statement of open use in this review.

GOES-16 backfill uploads run to 2025-04-17 (ACHAC key 2025/049/19). The newest ACHAC object by scan time is 2025/097/18 (2025-04-07). Registry: GOES-16 distribution is turned off after the GOES-19 transition.

GOES-18 extents: pixel-centre 175.91 E to -89.91 (the first report's -184.1 is 175.9 E unwrapped); file attributes 175.62358 E and -89.62357 differ by 0.29 deg. GOES-19 file west extent differs from pixel centres by 0.7 deg and from pixel edges by 1.1 deg.
confirmed: Cadence: 300 s steps for ACHAC, CMIPC, CODC, MCMIPC and ACHA2KMC; 600 s for ACHAF; 12 and 6 scans per hour (hours 00-01, both satellites); 290 day folders for 2026 (GOES-19 and GOES-18).
GOES-16 has 0 objects dated 2026 in all 102 top-level prefixes.
Grid: ACHAC 300 x 500 at 10.02 km (0.000280 rad); CMIPC and CODC 1500 x 2500 at 2.004 km (0.000056 rad).
CMI int16, scale 0.06145332, offset 89.62, fill -1, valid 0-4095 (89.62-341.27 K). Montana 2 km: 44,363 cells, all valid, DQF 0, BT 216.21-284.49 K, p50 275.64 K.
ACHAC HT scale 0.3052037, fill 65535, valid 0-65530. CONUS 102,968 valid = cloud_pixels = DQF 0 count; Montana 733 of 1,777; 0.71% of CONUS valid cells.
percent_good_quality_qf 0.694969 = 102,968 / (150,000 - 1,838 fill), exact.

Off-Earth cells: ACHAC 1,887 of 150,000; CMIPC 47,162 of 3,750,000. Own GOES-R inverse vs PROJ: ACHAC 9.7e-11 deg lat and 7.1e-10 deg lon; CMIPC 3.4e-10 and 2.6e-9. Image centre attribute 30.083 N, -87.097 W reproduced.

CODC Montana: 7,237 valid (16.3%), p10/p50/p90 0.12/0.32/0.88, max 16.0, DQF 133 x7,078 (degraded, cloud-phase-ice bit 128), DQF 1 x159. CONUS 1,961,560 valid; 55.67% degraded. File night min/max/mean 0.0/16.0/4.8758 confirmed.
Exact per-scan totals for GOES-19 scan 01:41:17: 62,415,370 bytes (16 CMIPC bands) and 26,145,976 bytes (7 ACHA inputs).
ATBD v3.0 (July 2012) section 1.6, printed p.12: 'The ACHA is responsible for estimation of vertical extent for all cloudy ABI pixels.' (verbatim).
Licence banner 'Unclassified data.  Access is restricted to approved users only.' present in ACHAC (GOES-18 and GOES-19), CMIPC C13, CODC and ACHA2KMC.
Registry sentences (summarising fetch): 'NOAA data disseminated through NODD are open to the public and can be used as desired.'; attribution sentence; GOES-16 distribution turned off.

CORS on 5 objects (GOES-19 ACHAC and CMIPC, GOES-18 CMIPC and CODC, GOES-16 2023 ACHAC): Access-Control-Allow-Origin * with an Origin header, including an unrelated origin; none without Origin; preflight Max-Age 3000; 'range' allowed. No Access-Control-Expose-Headers, so Content-Range is not readable from script.
GOES-18 Montana: 2,041 cells; 859 valid (42.09%); p50 9,195.2 m; DQF 0 on valid cells. CONUS 116,965 valid (01:41).
Billings: 2 km BT 278.28 K. VZA GOES-19 62.1 deg, GOES-18 59.7 deg (within 0.15 deg of first report). Flat-Earth 10 km: 18.9 / 17.1 km.
ACHAF full disk 1.59 MB per 10 min (GOES-19), 1.63 MB (GOES-18).
unverified: Cause of warm BT at valid high tops (CONUS 10-20 km medians 257-268 K in ACHAC, ACHA2KMC and GOES-18). Thin cloud, retrieval bias and sampling are not separated. The bucket top level has no CONUS cloud-top temperature product (only ACHTF and ACHTM) to cross-check.
Whether 10 km HT is a 5x5 block average (ATBD) or a point value (file cell_methods).
Legal scope of 'Unclassified data. Access is restricted to approved users only.': a search found no GOES-specific source. Redistribution is unresolved, and the data.gov CC0 entry conflicts.
Causes of the 0.012 K band 13 min/max gap, of the COD 16.0 cap, and of the extent-attribute mismatch.
ACHA2KMC was decoded for 2026 scenes only. 2023 grid and latency were not opened; the 2023-03-24 start comes from listing (288 scans on 2023-03-24, none on 2023-03-11).
Browser-side NetCDF/HDF5 decoding was not tested. CORS shows the objects are fetchable, not that a page can decode them.
DQF value 4 (opaque retrieval) was not observed in any 2026 sample.
Age-at-listing values are time-dependent and were not re-measured.

refuted_claims: Day mean 21.3 MB per step and about 640 MB/h: a 2-hour window (62 steps, 00:00:39-02:04:39 UTC 2026-10-17), not a day. Whole days are 19.8 MB (2025-06-15) and 24.9 MB (2026-10-16) per step, about 594-746 MB/h.
Latency 35-99 s as a general range: true only at 02:04:39 on 2026-10-17; the whole day 2026-10-16 spans 29-120 s per object.
8 bits per value for MESH: false for the 2025-06-15 MESH file (16 bits, 345 distinct values); true for the 2026 files checked.
'CONUS' labels on whole-grid shares: those figures are the 7000x3500 file grid (incl. ocean, Canada, Mexico); the contiguous-US box gives 14.4% for MESH and RQI -3.
Event peak 23:12:41 and 72.5 dBZ at 22:24:41 as day peaks: these are maxima of the 0-offset 12-minute sample; the 3-offset sample gives 6,546 pts >= 35 dBZ at 23:06:42 and 73.5 dBZ at 22:30:42.

'NOAA states no retention period' and NOAA-attributed reuse wording: no retention statement on the registry page; the NOAA NODD page read by WebFetch lacks the reuse wording (it appears on the AWS registry page only).
README sec. 4 'MRMS carries its own no-coverage mask' (plan text): no mask product exists; the -999 code in each 3D file is the only coverage signal, and its meaning is unverified for v12.
corrections: Cadence '62 intervals today' is the 00:00-02:04 window (mean 120.00 s, sd 2.98, range 113-130 s, exact); whole day 2026-10-16 sd 2.5 s, range 109-128 s; RQI exactly 120 s.
2025-06-15 archive LastModified is an upload time (per-level medians 870-1,295 s after valid time), not real-time latency.
GRIB units read 'unknown' for every product (reflectivity, MESH, RQI): 'dBZ' and 'mm' are inferred.
03.00 4x4 sub-box shares reproduce within 0.3 points; the previous split was not stated.

-999 and -3 sets are approximately, not exactly, static: Montana -999 counts are equal at the 2026 times (206,990 at 3 km), but grid-wide -999 differs by 24,623 px (3 km, 2026) and 175,928 px (2025 event).
CORS preflight now tested (previously 'not tested'): Allow-Origin *, Allow-Methods HEAD, GET, Max-Age 3000, Allow-Headers range when requested.

Folded to fit 20 KB: verified facts duplicated in review.confirmed or unverified were merged or removed (3D levels, name checks, Montana box, cell size, live freshness, update cycle, grid cross-check, gzip, 00:18 jitter, heightAboveSea, sentinel leads); four Montana and three event facts merged. Evidence file is 19,849 bytes.
confirmed: 243 prefixes; 33 levels 00.50-19.00 km (0.25, 0.5 and 1 km steps); no Coverage or Mask names; RadarQualityIndex only _00.00; MESH_Max 30-1440 min.
Grid 7000x3500, 0.01 deg, index = row x 7000 + col (five points); Billings 0.383 km; Montana box 557,264 pts; cells 1.112 km N-S, 0.758 km E-W at 47 N.
grid_png; 16-bit reflectivity; 0.1 dBZ steps; heightAboveSea 500-19000 m; 02:04:39 33-level total 20,013,085 B (matches listing); gunzip adds 11.4% for 00.50 (341,919 B).
Montana shares at 02:04:39; zero valid dBZ at 2026-10-16 12:56:36; 2025-06-15 23:12:41 Montana counts (four levels); MESH event counts.
02:04:39 MESH, RQI and latency values; 00:18 stamp jitter (00.50 at 00:18:38, others 00:18:40); live stamps 02:28:41 and 02:26:40 existed.
